items.title: The Knight's Leap
items.question: Abraham raises the knife over Isaac at God's command — murder by every universal ethic, faith by Kierkegaard's. What does the leap of faith suspend?
items.correctExplanation: The universal's claims — teleological suspension: the single individual stands higher than the general for a higher telos. Ethics relativized, not abolished.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is the universal claims of ethics. God, feelings, and physics miss it: Abraham keeps faith while breaking morality's universality. Suspension elevates the single above the general paradoxically.
items.lessonContent:
Singles can stand above generals paradoxically.
Suspension elevates; it never abolishes.
Higher telos relativizes universal claims.
Faith begins where ethics ends, terrifyingly.
Share this: feel one paradox's weight today.

items.title: The Double Movement
items.question: The knight of infinite resignation renounces the finite nobly; the knight of faith makes a second movement — receiving finitude back by virtue of the absurd. What distinguishes faith from resignation?
choices: The second movement of joyful reception
items.correctAnswer: The second movement of joyful reception
items.correctExplanation: Joyful reception back — resignation stops at renunciation; faith proceeds to receive the finite again, absurdly. Princes and tax collectors dance while philosophers only renounce.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is the second movement of joyful reception. Knowledge, testimony, and age miss it: both knights renounce, only one receives. Faith's extra step looks exactly like bourgeois contentment — invisibly.
items.lessonContent:
Receiving back exceeds renouncing nobly.
Second movements hide inside ordinary joy.
Resignation stops; faith proceeds absurdly.
Invisible crowns beat visible sackcloth.
Share this: receive one finite joy absurdly.

items.title: The Inward Truth
items.question: 'Truth is subjectivity' — Kierkegaard locates religious truth in passionate inward appropriation, not detached approximation. What decides truth here?
choices: How passionately the self holds it
items.correctAnswer: How passionately the self holds it
items.correctExplanation: Passionate holding — inwardness decides where objectivity abstains. Faith's truth lives in the how of holding, never the what of content.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is how passionately the self holds it. Consensus, antiquity, and proofs measure objective approximations; faith demands subjective appropriation. The knower's posture constitutes the known.
items.lessonContent:
Postures constitute what they hold.
Holding-how outweighs content-what in faith.
Approximation abstains where passion decides.
Inwardness is truth's religious mode.
Share this: hold one thing passionately.

items.title: The Uncertain Fire
items.question: Faith, Kierkegaard says, holds fast with maximum passion precisely where objective certainty is minimal. What ratio defines belief?
items.correctExplanation: Maximum passion, minimum certainty — uncertainty is faith's oxygen, not its enemy. Objective doubts feed subjective fire.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is maximum passion with minimum certainty. Proportional belief describes science; faith inverts the ratio deliberately. Uncertainty fuels what evidence would extinguish.
items.lessonContent:
Uncertainty fuels faith it would starve in science.
Ratios invert between knowing and believing.
Doubts feed fires they threaten elsewhere.
Passion peaks where proof runs dry.
Share this: burn brightly past evidence once.

items.title: The Seducer's Rotation
items.question: The aesthete survives boredom by 'rotation of crops' — varying soil, not harvesting meaning. Don Juan serializes pleasures to dodge emptiness. What strategy is this?
items.correctExplanation: Systematic novelty — crop rotation for the soul: change fields, never farm. Boredom managed, meaning never met.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is systematic novelty against boredom. Commitment, devotion, and revolution miss the aesthetic: variety without depth, motion without arrival. Rotation postpones the despair it cannot cure.
items.lessonContent:
Variety postpones despairs it cannot cure.
Motion differs from arrival entirely.
Rotation manages what commitment would heal.
Novelty systems defend against depth.
Share this: farm one field deeply today.

items.title: The Married Judge
items.question: Judge William defends marriage, vocation, and continuity against aesthetic flightiness — choosing oneself through commitment. What stage does he voice?
items.correctExplanation: The ethical — commitment, continuity, choosing the self one already is. Marriage as metaphysics: repetition with meaning.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is the ethical stage. Aesthetic flees, religious transcends, irony observes — the Judge commits. Vocation and wedding ring outrank infinite possibility here.
items.lessonContent:
Commitment outranks possibility ethically.
Continuity dignifies repetition with meaning.
Choosing oneself beats sampling selves.
Rings outweigh rotations in this stage.
Share this: choose one continuity today.

items.title: The Suffering Saint
items.question: Beyond ethics lies the religious: Job's suffering, Abraham's paradox — God relating where reason resigns. What marks this highest stage?
items.correctExplanation: Paradoxical God-relation — suffering and absurdity as meeting places. Reason resigns; faith relates anyway.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is paradoxical relation to the absolute. Morals, wealth, and applause belong to lower stages: religion begins where ethics breaks. Job suffers, Abraham lifts knives — both relate past reason.
items.lessonContent:
Religion begins where ethics breaks down.
Suffering becomes meeting place, not problem.
Absurdity hosts what reason cannot.
Relate past understanding's border.
Share this: relate past one border.

items.title: The Fatal Imbalance
items.question: Despair, in The Sickness Unto Death, is misrelation in the self's synthesis — finite/infinite, temporal/eternal, freedom/necessity out of joint. What is despair structurally?
items.correctExplanation: Misrelated synthesis — the self unbalanced across its constitutive polarities. Despair is architecture, not accident.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is a misrelated synthesis of opposites. Chemicals, punishments, and genes miss the structure: selves are syntheses, and syntheses can mistune. Diagnose architecture before chemistry.
items.lessonContent:
Selves are syntheses that can mistune.
Polarities need balancing, not amputating.
Architecture precedes chemistry in despair.
Diagnose structures before prescribing pills.
Share this: tune one polarity today.

items.title: The Relating Relation
items.question: 'The self is a relation that relates itself to itself' — a synthesis conscious of synthesizing. What makes human selfhood unique here?
items.correctExplanation: Self-conscious synthesis — relating to one's own relating: spirit as reflexive loop. Bodies, deeds, and grammar miss the reflexive core.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is self-conscious synthesis of opposites. The formula's third term (relating-to-relating) makes spirit: finite-infinite syntheses aware of themselves. Loops, not lumps, define selves.
items.lessonContent:
Loops define selves; lumps merely occupy.
Relating-to-relating makes spirit happen.
Reflexivity crowns synthesis with selfhood.
Third terms transform pairs into persons.
Share this: relate to one relating.

items.title: The Finite Fever
items.question: Despair of finitude lacks infinitude — drowning in facts, deadlines, probabilities, 'the probable' as prison. What does this despair miss?
items.correctExplanation: Possibility beyond calculation — finitude despair suffocates in probable actualities. Facts need windows, not just walls.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is the infinite: possibility beyond calculation. Information, schedules, and willpower feed the prison: more facts fatten finitude. Despair of finitude needs air, not data.
items.lessonContent:
Facts fatten finitude's prison daily.
Possibility airs what probability seals.
Windows beat walls for despairing minds.
Calculate less; imagine more.
Share this: open one impossible window.

items.title: The Infinite Drift
items.question: Despair of infinitude lacks finitude — fantasies, feelings, and abstractions with no actuality to anchor them. What does this despair need?
items.correctExplanation: Finitude — limits, decisions, actual mornings. Infinite drift needs ballast, not bigger sails.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is finitude: actuality, limits, decisions. Visions, intensities, and sittings feed the drift: abstraction unmoored is despair's other wing. Anchor in actuality to fly at all.
items.lessonContent:
Abstraction unmoored is despair's wing.
Ballast precedes flight always.
Decisions anchor drifting infinities.
Actual mornings ground possible ones.
Share this: decide one actual thing.

items.title: The Unknowing Sick
items.question: The worst despair, Kierkegaard says, is being unaware of being in despair — spiritlessness mistaking itself for health. What makes it worst?
items.correctExplanation: Unawareness — unfelt sickness seeks no cure: the spiritless call it realism. Conscious despair at least knows its address.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is its unawareness of itself. Symptoms, rarity, and noise miss it: unknown illness never consults doctors. Spiritlessness posing as health is despair's perfect camouflage.
items.lessonContent:
Unknown illnesses never seek cures.
Camouflage perfects what pain would expose.
Realism poses mask spiritlessness often.
Consciousness, even pained, beats numbness.
Share this: check one numbness honestly.

items.title: The Crowd Verdict
items.question: 'The crowd is untruth' — Kierkegaard insists truth needs the single individual; majorities decide nothing about the eternal. Where does truth reside?
items.correctExplanation: With the single individual — crowds vote on matters where voting is nonsense. Eternal questions need solitary deciders.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is with the single individual. Majorities, institutions, and volumes miss it: truth doesn't poll well. One person can be right against ten thousand — categorically.
items.lessonContent:
Polls malfunction on eternal questions.
Solitary deciders carry truth sometimes.
Majorities decide nothing ultimate ever.
One against ten thousand can win truly.
Share this: stand singly once today.

items.title: The Leveling Press
items.question: The daily press, Kierkegaard warned, levels all excellence into equally consumable chatter — no one may stand out. What does leveling destroy?
items.correctExplanation: Distinction itself — leveling makes eminence unreadable: all flattened to audience level. Chatter consumes what admiration would crown.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is distinction itself. Profits, literacy, and post miss it: the press's leveling abstraction dissolves qualitatively different into quantitatively same. Excellence becomes content.
items.lessonContent:
Abstractions dissolve qualitative differences.
Content flattens what admiration crowned.
Leveling reads eminence as noise.
Distinction needs defenders, not just admirers.
Share this: admire one distinction fully.

items.title: The Passionless Age
items.question: The present age, Kierkegaard charged, is reflective and passionless — all deliberation, no enthusiasm, envy as its only unity. What characterizes it?
items.correctExplanation: Reflection without passion — thinking that never bleeds into action. Deliberation replaces devotion; envy replaces admiration.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is reflection without passion. Fervor, labor, and crowds miss it: the age thinks everything and does nothing. Passionless reflection is the specific modern sickness.
items.lessonContent:
Thinking-that-never-bleeds sickens ages.
Deliberation replaces devotion silently.
Envy unites where admiration divided.
Passionlessness is the precise diagnosis.
Share this: bleed into one action today.

items.title: The Envious Glue
items.question: In passionless ages, Kierkegaard says, envy becomes the negative unifying principle — all secretly level all. What binds such societies?
items.correctExplanation: Mutual envy — secret leveling pacts: none shall rise, all shall watch. Negative unity binds tighter than positive.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is mutual envy. Admiration, worship, and enterprise unite positively; envy unites by shared resentment of eminence. Glue made of grievance holds firmest.
items.lessonContent:
Grievance glues firmer than admiration.
Leveling pacts bind secretly always.
Negative unity outlasts positive easily.
Envy organizes where love disperses.
Share this: admire instead of envying once.

items.title: The Midwife Method
items.question: Truth that concerns existing — how to live — cannot be taught directly but must be midwifed: the learner gives birth herself. What communication does this require?
items.correctExplanation: Indirect maieutic communication — Socratic midwifery for existential truth. Direct teaching delivers information; only indirection delivers transformation.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is indirect, maieutic communication. Lectures inform, repetitions drill, exams test — none beget. Existing-truths need birthing assistance, never prefab delivery.
items.lessonContent:
Birthing beats delivering for living truths.
Midwives assist; lecturers merely inform.
Indirection respects learner inwardness.
Prefab truths transform nobody ever.
Share this: midwife one insight today.

items.title: The Dizzy Edge
items.question: Anxiety, Kierkegaard writes, is 'the dizziness of freedom' — staring into possibility's abyss where one can choose. What causes this vertigo?
items.correctExplanation: Possibility's abyss — freedom vertiginizes because everything might be chosen. Dizziness measures openness, not altitude.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is freedom's abyss of possibility. Cliffs, sugar, and sleep miss it: the precipice is internal — 'I can' stretching infinitely. Vertigo gauges freedom's depth precisely.
items.lessonContent:
Openness vertiginizes more than heights.
'I can' stretches infinitely inward.
Dizziness gauges freedom's depth well.
Abysses internal dwarf external ones.
Share this: peer into one possibility.

items.title: The Necessary Offense
items.question: The God-man paradox necessarily offends reason — offense isn't a bug but the mark of encountering transcendence. What does offense signal?
items.correctExplanation: Genuine paradox-encounter — offense is reason's correct response to the absurd. Smooth doctrines never touched transcendence.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is genuine encounter with paradox. Falsity, preaching, and translation miss it: offense certifies contact with what exceeds understanding. The unoffended never met the paradox.
items.lessonContent:
Offense certifies transcendent contact.
Smoothness signals absence of paradox.
Reason rightly chokes on infinity.
Unoffended means unencountered here.
Share this: be offended productively once.

items.title: The Doubled Return
items.question: Job loses everything, then receives everything back doubled — not recollection of the past but repetition forward. What does genuine repetition give?
items.correctExplanation: The same made new — repetition isn't recollection backward but reception forward: Job's doubled goods are new gifts, not returned loans.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is the same goods made new. Restoration, nostalgia, and compensation miss it: repetition moves forward where recollection looks back. Doubled returns are new creations.
items.lessonContent:
Forward reception beats backward recollection.
New gifts differ from returned loans.
Doubling signifies creation, not refund.
Repeat forward, never merely recall.
Share this: receive one return as new.

items.title: The Patient Soul
items.question: 'In patience you will gain your souls' — Kierkegaard reads patience not as passive waiting but as active soul-winning. What does patience gain?
items.correctExplanation: One's soul itself — patience as self-acquisition: enduring time without fleeing it wins the endurer. Waiting works when waiting wills.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is one's soul itself. Rewards, approval, and power miss it: patience gains the waiter, not the waited-for. Soul-winning happens in duration endured.
items.lessonContent:
Waiting wills what fleeing forfeits.
Duration endured wins endurers.
Souls gained through patience kept.
Active waiting beats passive killing-time.
Share this: gain one minute soulfully.

items.title: The Knowing Ignorance
items.question: Socrates claimed wisdom in knowing that he knew nothing, while sophists professed omniscience. What makes ignorance philosophical?
items.correctExplanation: Awareness of not knowing — examined ignorance opens inquiry where professed knowledge closes it. Socratic wisdom is meta-knowing.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is awareness of not knowing. Skepticism denies, doctrines stockpile, debates perform — only owned ignorance inquires. Sophists knew everything and learned nothing.
items.lessonContent:
Owned ignorance inquires; professed knowledge rests.
Meta-knowing beats knowing in philosophy.
Sophists stockpile; Socrates empties usefully.
Examinations begin with confessed gaps.
Share this: confess one fertile ignorance.

items.title: The Silent Knight
items.question: Agamemnon can speechify his sacrifice; Abraham must stay silent — faith speaks no universal tongue. What can the knight of faith never do?
items.correctExplanation: Speak his justification aloud — ethics demands communicability; faith transcends it. Silence is the paradox's native tongue.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is speak his justification aloud. Anguish felt, commands obeyed, love intact — yet no universal words exist for the act. Tragic heroes explain; knights of faith cannot.
items.lessonContent:
Universals demand speech; paradoxes forbid it.
Silence is faith's native tongue here.
Tragic heroes explain; knights cannot.
Incommunicability marks transcendence exactly.
Share this: keep one silence faithfully.

items.title: The Chosen Choice
items.question: Either/Or's deepest choice isn't pleasure versus duty but choosing versus drifting — willing to will at all. What comes before every option?
items.correctExplanation: To choose at all — meta-choice precedes content: drifters never reach options. Willing to will is freedom's first act.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is to choose at all. Pleasures, wealth, and youth are contents; choosing is the container. Aesthetes drift among options they never elect.
items.lessonContent:
Containers precede contents in freedom.
Drifters never reach real options.
Willing-to-will is freedom's first act.
Meta-choices govern all object choices.
Share this: elect one option deliberately.

items.title: The Fixed Cage
items.question: One despair insists everything is necessary — nothing can be otherwise, effort is theater. Against such fatalism, what is missing?
items.correctExplanation: Possibility — necessity-everywhere is mood posing as metaphysics. Denied openings remain open regardless.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is possibility. Effort-theater excuses surrender in advance; fatalism mistakes feeling for fact. Openings denied are openings still.
items.lessonContent:
Necessity claimed everywhere suffocates action.
Theater-effort beliefs excuse all surrender.
Openings denied are openings still.
Fatalism mistakes mood for metaphysics.
Share this: open one denied maybe today.
